summary: Added production infrastructure, request validation, rate limiting, and unified auth for the Next.js app.
commandsRun: apt-get update && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y nodejs npm
export PATH="/tmp/node20/bin:$PATH" && npm install zod eslint eslint-config-next && npm uninstall @auth/prisma-adapter
export PATH="/tmp/node20/bin:$PATH" && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/__tests__/env.test.ts src/__tests__/validation.test.ts src/__tests__/rate-limit.test.ts

export PATH="/tmp/node20/bin:$PATH" && DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/gospeldrop NEXTAUTH_URL=https://gospeldrop.example.com NEXTAUTH_SECRET=super-secret-value-with-at-least-thirty-two-chars STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_1234567890 EMAIL_FROM=hello@gospeldrop.example.com npm run build
testsRun: export PATH="/tmp/node20/bin:$PATH" && DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/gospeldrop NEXTAUTH_URL=https://gospeldrop.example.com NEXTAUTH_SECRET=super-secret-value-with-at-least-thirty-two-chars STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_1234567890 EMAIL_FROM=hello@gospeldrop.example.com npm run build
knownIssues: Rate limiting uses in-memory middleware state, which is acceptable for a single Node process but should be replaced with a shared store (for example Upstash Redis or Cloudflare KV) for horizontally scaled production deployments.
The verification environment required a local Node 20 runtime bootstrap because the base image shipped Node 18 while Vitest/Vite in this repo require Node 20+.
nextStep: Review and merge the PR, then provision real production secrets and replace the in-memory limiter with a shared backend before scaling out.
